title: Clerical Verdict and the Order to Dismember Mani Singh

blocks.text: Once Mani Singh refuses conversion and rejects compromise, the Nawab turns to qazis and mullas to frame the punishment in legal and religious terms. The Sikh prisoners remain firm, insisting that they will not abandon their path even under the threat of exemplary violence.

The verdict that emerges is designed to terrify. Mani Singh is sentenced to be dismembered limb by limb, a ruling that echoes the congregation’s earlier prophecy and transforms a court punishment into the literal fulfillment of words already spoken over him.

At the place of execution, Mani Singh shows unshaken composure and even corrects the executioners when they begin too crudely. By insisting that the sentence be carried out joint by joint, he reveals both the horror of the order and the extraordinary steadiness with which he meets it.
